# Baseline UI

Enforces an opinionated UI baseline to prevent AI-generated interface slop.

## How to use

- `/baseline-ui`
  Apply these constraints to any UI work in this conversation.

- `/baseline-ui <file>`
  Review the file against all constraints below and output:
  - violations (quote the exact line/snippet)
  - why it matters (1 short sentence)
  - a concrete fix (code-level suggestion)

## Stack

- MUST use Tailwind CSS defaults unless custom values already exist or are explicitly requested
- MUST use `motion/react` (formerly `framer-motion`) when JavaScript animation is required
- SHOULD use `tw-animate-css` for entrance and micro-animations in Tailwind CSS
- MUST use `cn` utility (`clsx` + `tailwind-merge`) for class logic

## Components

- MUST use accessible component primitives for anything with keyboard or focus behavior (`Base UI`, `React Aria`, `Radix`)
- MUST use the project’s existing component primitives first
- NEVER mix primitive systems within the same interaction surface
- SHOULD prefer [`Base UI`](https://base-ui.com/react/components) for new primitives if compatible with the stack
- MUST add an `aria-label` to icon-only buttons
- NEVER rebuild keyboard or focus behavior by hand unless explicitly requested

## Interaction

- MUST use an `AlertDialog` for destructive or irreversible actions
- SHOULD use structural skeletons for loading states
- NEVER use `h-screen`, use `h-dvh`
- MUST respect `safe-area-inset` for fixed elements
- MUST show errors next to where the action happens
- NEVER block paste in `input` or `textarea` elements

## Animation

- NEVER add animation unless it is explicitly requested
- MUST animate only compositor props (`transform`, `opacity`)
- NEVER animate layout properties (`width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin`, `padding`)
- SHOULD avoid animating paint properties (`background`, `color`) except for small, local UI (text, icons)
- SHOULD use `ease-out` on entrance
- NEVER exceed `200ms` for interaction feedback
- MUST pause looping animations when off-screen
- SHOULD respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
- NEVER introduce custom easing curves unless explicitly requested
- SHOULD avoid animating large images or full-screen surfaces

## Typography

- MUST use `text-balance` for headings and `text-pretty` for body/paragraphs
- MUST use `tabular-nums` for data
- SHOULD use `truncate` or `line-clamp` for dense UI
- NEVER modify `letter-spacing` (`tracking-*`) unless explicitly requested

## Layout

- MUST use a fixed `z-index` scale (no arbitrary `z-*`)
- SHOULD use `size-*` for square elements instead of `w-*` + `h-*`

## Performance

- NEVER animate large `blur()` or `backdrop-filter` surfaces
- NEVER apply `will-change` outside an active animation
- NEVER use `useEffect` for anything that can be expressed as render logic

## Design

- NEVER use gradients unless explicitly requested
- NEVER use purple or multicolor gradients
- NEVER use glow effects as primary affordances
- SHOULD use Tailwind CSS default shadow scale unless explicitly requested
- MUST give empty states one clear next action
- SHOULD limit accent color usage to one per view
- SHOULD use existing theme or Tailwind CSS color tokens before introducing new ones

name: component-canvas
description: Build a full-screen, interactive canvas to explore existing UI components and their variants with pan and zoom.
---

# Component canvas

Build a canvas that shows the project's existing components as they really behave. The canvas wraps components. It never changes them.

## Ground rules

- Do not modify component source, exports, styles, hooks, or behavior to make the canvas work. Components must not import or depend on canvas code.
- Do not patch libraries, browser APIs, rendered component DOM, or portal roots.
- Show only the components the user asked for. Adding components, installing dependencies, changing a component's design, or making the canvas public requires permission first.
- Keep existing access controls.
- Leave unrelated work alone. If removing an earlier canvas integration, undo only its changes to components.
- Follow any restrictions on commands, browser access, dependencies, and edits.

## Before building

Read the repository conventions, routes, component public APIs, design tokens, and test setup. Use the existing framework and libraries.

Ask the user only when the answer changes what gets built or touches shared code: which components are in scope, whether a new dependency is acceptable, or whether a live service may be previewed. For everything else, choose a sensible default, state it in the report, and proceed.

## Build order

1. Add a minimal canvas route or entry point with one group and one component. Confirm it works.
2. Add the remaining groups with sample data.
3. Add variant comparisons, then advanced gestures and persistence, one feature at a time.

Keep canvas code in one place. Check imports and package exports when moving files. Follow the project's language, validation, and test conventions. Do not add architectural layers or directory names the project does not already use.

Keep layout and camera logic separate from sample data and component source.

## Layout

- Fill the viewport with a plain background.
- If the project already supports light and dark themes, add an accessible toggle using its existing theme API. Apply the selected theme to the canvas and native portals. If theme support is absent, omit the toggle. Do not invent themes or change component styles.
- Give every group the same padding, radius, and thin dashed border, subtle but visible in both themes. Use an existing muted color at roughly 25% opacity for borders. Place its plain title 8px above the border, using the muted text color without opacity.
- Use wide groups with equal-width example slots filling each row. Wrap when needed and keep generous horizontal and vertical gaps within and between groups. Spread the layout without enlarging components.
- Groups cannot be dragged. Their positions need not be hard-coded. Measure their actual bounds, including title, border, and padding. Ignore rendering-containment placeholders (empty boxes that reserve space before content renders), since they do not reflect real content size.
- Omit background dots, decorative cards, page menus, instruction banners, selection tools, and block editing. Component cards and menus may appear as examples.

## Variants

- Show every supported named variant and useful state within the requested scope. Read the public APIs for styles, text and icon sizes, orientation, placement, alignment, modality, and collapse modes.
- Include useful content and composition examples.
- Do not invent variants or generate every prop combination. List what was omitted and why.
- Compare one prop or feature at a time. Hold everything else constant: same wrapper, same sample data, same text, icons, theme, and spacing.
- Change the style variant only in style comparisons. Size, state, placement, and other comparisons use a single style, usually the default.

Example: in a size comparison, every button reads "Continue" and uses `variant="default"`. Only `size` changes. The style comparison changes `variant` and keeps size and text the same.

- Keep the component's own state styling (disabled opacity, checked color). Examples respond to input unless they show a disabled or read-only state.
- Test hover, focus, and pressed states through real pointer and keyboard input, not added classes.
- For portal examples, use the same trigger each time. Do not force several modals open at once.
- Keep a variant list and coverage tests. Use types if the project supports them.
- If a component cannot show a responsive or visual case, explain the limit. Do not change the component to fake it.

## Interactions

- Clicks, text selection, typing, button and switch activation, focus, and nested scrolling must keep working.
- Canvas shortcuts (Space, arrows, Escape, native undo) apply to the canvas shell only. They must not take those keys away from preview controls.
- Handle preview navigation in the canvas host. Links to canvas groups move the camera instead of scrolling the page. Define what happens to links that leave the canvas, including links inside portals. Do not change component links or router internals.
- Portals stay in their native roots at screen-space size. Let the library handle positioning and modal focus. Use public container options only when needed. Check positioning and clickable areas under canvas transforms. If they break, report it or propose a separate preview document. Do not patch components.
- The canvas has no undo/redo, editing shortcuts, or history.

## Safety for previews

Make each preview safe before it mounts:

- Use providers with test data, mock services, or existing callback props to block live calls and real writes.
- Static demo assets and local fixtures are fine.
- Never use production credentials or data.
- If safe isolation is not available, omit the live example and explain why. A separate document alone does not make a preview safe.

## Camera

- Mouse and trackpad: pan, and zoom around the cursor. Touch: pan and pinch.
- Start ordinary pan on empty canvas space. Keep native gestures inside previews and portals.
- Do not cancel events broadly, and do not put `touch-action: none` on interactive content.
- Handle pointer count changes, cancellation, lost capture, window blur, and hidden tabs. Release captures and clean up listeners, observers, timers, and animation frames on teardown.
- Apply gesture transforms at most once per animation frame. Avoid alternating layout reads and writes.
- Prevent group overlap when content expands or the viewport resizes. Avoid layout loops and unnecessary movement. Fit after layout settles. Fitting never rearranges groups.
- Move the camera to reveal keyboard focus outside the visible area. Native page scrolling must not move the canvas.
- Keyboard camera navigation works, with visible focus on canvas controls.
- Provide fit-all and reset icon buttons with accessible names. Keep them reachable even when the view is lost.
- Validate camera values and keep them within bounds.

## Persistence

- Save only the camera, in a versioned format, under a storage key per project or workspace.
- Handle malformed or oversized data, unavailable storage, and quota errors.
- Migrate known older formats. For unknown formats, use safe defaults and discard old group positions and history.
- Reset restores the camera only. It does not clear preview state or drafts.

## Checks

Run the repository's checks when allowed. Then, in the browser, confirm:

- The route mounts, imports and exports resolve, and the console shows no errors.
- Component source is unchanged.
- Listed variants appear, omissions are explained, groups have dashed borders, and non-style comparisons use one style.
- Keyboard camera navigation and visible focus work. Preview controls keep their native shortcuts and gestures.
- Nested scrolling, portal positioning, clickable areas, and modal focus work at several zoom levels and viewport sizes.
- Pan and pinch survive pointer changes and cancellation. Teardown releases resources.
- Groups do not overlap after expansion or resize. Fit works, and offscreen focus reveals correctly.
- Camera persists across reload. A storage failure falls back safely. Reset keeps preview drafts. Drafts need not survive reload unless requested.
- Groups cannot be dragged. The canvas has no undo/redo.
- Previews use safe test data and make no real project or account writes.

A check counts as passing only if it was run. If a check was skipped, say so.

## Report

End every build or review with these headings:

- **Changed:** files and what changed in each. Note any component changes (there should be none).
- **Checks run:** each check and its result.
- **Not working or not tested:** known gaps, omitted variants and why, and anything unverified.
- **Decisions made:** defaults chosen without asking.

Do not describe the implementation as verified or the template as ready unless every check above passed.

---
name: create-canvas
description: Build a freeform canvas to explore, compare, and iterate on anything.
---

# Create canvas

Build a freeform workspace for exploration and iteration through conversation. The model changes content in source files. The canvas makes that content live, named, movable, and easy to reference.

## Start with the project

- Read repository rules, routes, component APIs, themes, design tokens, and tests.
- Look for an existing canvas before creating another.
- Use the project's framework, components, typography, design tokens, themes, and access controls.
- Respect restrictions on edits, commands, and browser access.
- Ask before changing scope, adding dependencies, changing shared code, or exposing the canvas publicly.
- If safe isolation is unclear, ask before proceeding. Never mount an unsafe preview.
- Choose sensible defaults for other decisions. Do not ask the user to repeat clear requests.
- Keep canvas code together. Separate camera and placement logic from previews, test data, and their registry. Do not build a framework.
- Start with one safe live preview, a readable label, and a separate move handle. Make sure that it mounts.
- Add the registry and requested content next. Then add copying, camera controls, existing themes, and saved layout.

## Keep content in source

A registry is a typed list of canvas items. Each entry defines a stable ID, unique readable name, component, safe test data, initial position, and dimensions.

- Keep the registry easy to find. Adding an item must not require changes to the camera or gesture code.
- Add, duplicate, rename, and remove items through source edits. Do not add runtime editor controls or delete shortcuts.
- Keep membership, names, dimensions, and implementations in source. Browser storage must not create or hide items.
- Never evaluate stored strings or model responses as code at runtime.
- Update the existing workspace for follow-up requests. Preserve names, IDs, positions, and unrelated experiments.
- If a reference is ambiguous, ask which item the user means.
- For “try another version,” preserve the original. Give each variation a new ID, unique readable name, and independent state.
- For “change this version,” update that item in place. Rename it only when asked.
- For removal requests, remove only the requested registry entry. Preserve shared components and unrelated work.
- When comparing one feature, keep other data, content, dimensions, and the global theme the same.
- For broader alternatives, name the layout differences. Do not create a full variant matrix unless requested.
- Place additions in nearby empty space using measured bounds. Reveal them with the camera without rearranging existing items or resetting the view.
- Preserve positions after content expansion, resizing, and reload. Allow intentional overlap. Keep move handles accessible when items overlap.

## Keep the workspace quiet

- Fill the viewport with a plain background, subtle preview boundaries, and minimal fixed controls.
- Use each preview's intended dimensions. Do not stretch content into oversized frames.
- Do not add decorative cards, banners, or background patterns.
- Put each name above its preview, such as `Pricing card · compact`. Do not use vague names or opaque IDs as labels.
- Give the name button behavior without button styling or a separate copy button.
- Copy the exact name on click, Enter, Space, or touch. Do not copy an ID, code, or URL.
- Explain copying on hover and keyboard focus. Hover alone must not copy. Touch activation must not require hover.
- Use the clipboard API when available. Announce brief “Copied” feedback only after success. Keep the name visible during feedback.
- If clipboard access fails or is unavailable, offer selectable text. Do not crash or claim success.
- Put a visible move handle beside the label. The label copies without dragging. The handle moves the item, not its body.
- Convert pointer movement to canvas coordinates at the current zoom.
- Support keyboard movement on the focused handle. Provide visible focus and accessible instructions.
- Use `cursor: default` on canvas navigation surfaces and handles, including during gestures.
- Preserve native text, link, input, and resize cursors inside previews. Do not apply cursor rules to all descendants.
- Include pan, zoom, fit-all, reset-camera, one global theme selector, and saved layout.
- Use the existing theme API for light, dark, and named themes. Apply the same theme to canvas controls, previews, menus, and dialogs.
- Do not invent themes or add per-preview themes. If themes are unsupported, omit the selector and explain why.
- If portal themes fail through public APIs, report the limit.
- Unless requested, omit resizing, width presets, comparison arrangements, drawing, connectors, catalogs, property editors, multi-selection, snapping, and undo/redo.
- For requested mobile or desktop previews, define their dimensions in the registry.

## Preserve live content

- Reuse production components through public APIs. Do not change their source, exports, hooks, or styles to support the canvas.
- Keep production components independent of canvas code.
- Keep experiments local to the canvas. Move them into production only when asked.
- Before mounting, use synthetic data, mock services, safe providers, and existing callbacks to prevent real requests and writes.
- Never use personal data or production credentials.
- If safe isolation is unavailable, omit the preview and explain why. An iframe or separate document alone does not provide isolation.
- Preserve clicking, typing, text selection, shortcuts, focus, nested scrolling, and touch input.
- Preserve the real behavior of disabled and read-only examples.
- Do not remount previews or erase input when moving items, copying names, changing themes, or changing the camera.
- Preview drafts do not need to survive reload.
- Keep portals in their native roots at screen-space size. Let the library manage positioning and modal focus.
- Use public container APIs only when needed. Make sure that portal alignment and clickable areas work at different zoom levels.
- If transforms break portals, report the limit or propose a separate preview document.
- Do not patch libraries, browser APIs, preview DOM, or portal roots.
- Define navigation in the canvas host, including links in portals. Do not change component links or router internals.
- Canvas-item links reveal their target instead of scrolling the page.
- Other navigation must not perform real project actions or silently lose the workspace.

## Keep gestures separate from preview input

- Support mouse drag to pan from empty space.
- Support Ctrl/Meta + wheel and trackpad pinch to zoom over empty space and previews.
- Keep the canvas point under the pointer fixed during wheel or pinch zoom.
- Provide zoom-in and zoom-out buttons and keyboard controls. Center their zoom on the viewport.
- Zoom smoothly in both directions without jumps or drift. Preserve item positions and preview state.
- Support touch pan and pinch where the browser permits them.
- Support keyboard camera navigation when the canvas shell has focus.
- Show visible keyboard focus on all canvas controls.
- Keep accessible fit-all and reset-camera controls fixed and reachable when items are offscreen.
- Run fit-all after layout settles. Fit the actual bounds, including each title, handle, and boundary. Do not rearrange items.
- Reset only the camera. Preserve membership, positions, themes, and drafts.
- Support Space + primary-button drag and middle-button drag to pan anywhere on the canvas, including over previews.
- Give explicit pan gestures priority over item movement and name copying.
- After a pan, do not activate controls, copy labels, follow links, or trigger middle-click autoscroll.
- If an interactive control or editable region has focus, do not arm Space-to-pan.
- Preserve Space activation of buttons and labels. Preserve preview arrow keys, Escape, and undo.
- Keep modal portals outside canvas gesture handling. Preserve their focus, backdrop behavior, and native controls.
- Support two-finger trackpad pan over empty space and previews.
- If a nested scroll area can scroll in the gesture direction, let it scroll. Otherwise, pan the canvas.
- Give modified-wheel and pinch zoom priority over scroll routing. Keep other portal scrolling native.
- Restrict event cancellation and touch restrictions to owned gestures. Do not disable native input across preview content.
- Use one finger to move items through their handles. Preserve ordinary one-finger preview interactions.
- Support two-finger canvas pan and pinch without breaking native preview gestures. Report browser limits instead of disabling preview touch.
- Track which gesture owns each interaction. Clear held keys on cancellation, window blur, and hidden tabs.
- Handle changes in pointer count, pointer cancellation, and lost pointer capture.
- On teardown, release captures and clean up listeners, observers, timers, and animation frames.
- While the route is active, apply `overscroll-behavior-x: none` to the document viewport and canvas scroll boundary.
- Block Chrome horizontal history swipes. An inner wrapper alone does not guarantee prevention.
- Restore prior document styles on teardown. Preserve nested horizontal scrolling, Back/Forward controls, and navigation shortcuts.
- Do not trap history with `pushState`, patch browser APIs, or leave permanent global handlers.
- Prevent native page scrolling from moving the canvas. Reveal offscreen keyboard focus through camera movement instead.
- Require finite, bounded camera coordinates, item positions, and zoom.
- Combine pointer and wheel updates into at most one transform write per animation frame.
- Keep active gesture values outside component-wide React state. Camera movement must not rerender previews.
- Update only canvas-owned wrappers. Do not change preview DOM or layout-affecting positions during gestures.
- Cache measured bounds. Refresh them together when content, dimensions, or layout changes.
- Ignore temporary rendering placeholders when measuring content bounds.
- Do not measure every preview each frame or alternate layout reads and writes.
- Save after gestures or with a bounded debounce. Do not write storage on every pointer event.
- On teardown, safely flush pending saves when possible.

name: create-design-md
description: Create or update a DESIGN.md from an existing product repository or public website. Use when asked to document an interface's design language, reconstruct its visual system, extract design tokens and guidance from current evidence, or give coding agents persistent UI context. Do not modify product source or promote accidental implementation patterns into design decisions.
---

# Create DESIGN.md

Create a `DESIGN.md` for one product or coherent website. Record the design language that governs it, not every value that happens to exist.

## Boundaries

- Modify only `DESIGN.md`. Do not change product source, dependencies, configuration, or generated files.
- Use the DESIGN.md format contract below. Do not invent a competing schema.
- Do not copy every discovered token or component into the document.
- Do not convert repetition, local styling, or visual preference into product intent.

## 1. Choose the mode

### Repository mode

Use when a local product repository is available. Create or update `DESIGN.md` at the root of the selected product.

If the repository contains multiple deployable products, select the one named by the user. If the request does not identify one and ownership is ambiguous, ask before writing.

Repository evidence may establish normative values, token names, component ownership, and documented rationale.

### URL mode

Use when the user provides a public URL without its source repository. Create a reconstructed `DESIGN.md` draft in the current workspace.

URL mode requires rendered browser access. Inspect the DOM, computed styles, and publicly loaded stylesheets at desktop and mobile widths. Screenshots may support interpretation but cannot establish exact values by themselves.

Inspect the supplied page and shared chrome. For a site-wide request, sample up to three same-origin pages that represent distinct templates.

URL evidence may establish only observable visual patterns and computed values. It cannot establish internal token names, component ownership, undocumented rationale, or whether a pattern is intentionally canonical.

If rendered inspection is unavailable, ask for screenshots or source files. Do not create a DESIGN.md from copy, metadata, or HTML structure alone.

Choose repository mode whenever source is available. A supplied URL may verify rendered presentation but does not replace repository evidence.

## Shared evidence pipeline

The modes differ only in how they collect evidence. They must use the same record and output pipeline:

```text
role → value → source → scope → recurrence → confidence
```

1. Collect evidence using the selected mode.
2. Record the source, scope, and recurrence for each candidate.
3. Normalize candidates into the DESIGN.md schema.
4. Omit candidates that are uncertain, local without a contract, or not implementation-relevant.
5. Validate frontmatter shape and export compatibility.
6. Write Markdown only after the normalized frontmatter passes.

Never let repository or URL evidence introduce a second token schema. The same flat token names, mapping-shaped typography, omission rules, and export gates apply to both modes.

The generated document is private until validation passes. Never return, display, or summarize a DESIGN.md draft before lint and export succeed. If validation reports an invalid shape or missing export category, rewrite the frontmatter and rerun; if the category cannot be repaired, remove it and report it as omitted.

## 2. Trace the evidence

In repository mode, inspect in this order:

1. Existing `DESIGN.md` and explicit repository guidance
2. Tokens, themes, variables, and global styles
3. Shared primitives and their variants
4. Representative routes and rendered consumers
5. Surface-local implementations

A source participates only when the selected product imports, references, inherits, or renders it. Exclude proposals, migrations, examples, generated outputs, legacy implementations, and similarly named packages unless the selected product uses them.

In URL mode, sample representative elements for:

- colors and surface roles
- typography roles
- spacing and layout
- borders, radii, and elevation
- navigation, buttons, inputs, cards, and repeated content structures
- desktop and mobile presentation

Prefer computed values and loaded CSS declarations over visual estimation.

Before drafting URL-mode prose or YAML, build a private evidence ledger for each sampled page and viewport. For each candidate, record: page, viewport, element role, computed property/value, and the matching loaded-CSS declaration or custom property when available. Inspect the public stylesheets loaded by the page, including custom properties and media-query rules; a stylesheet value is usable only when it is connected to a rendered element or recurs across the sampled pages.

Promote a URL value into DESIGN.md when either (a) the rendered computed value and a loaded declaration/custom property agree, or (b) the same computed value recurs for the same role across the required samples. If neither condition holds, omit the value. You may preserve an exposed custom-property name only when its declaration and rendered use are directly observable; do not invent semantic aliases from a raw value.

For every URL-mode claim, require all three proofs before writing it:

1. Observation: the pattern or value is visible or computed on the rendered page.
2. Basis: it is measured, or recurs across the required sampled pages/viewports.
3. Consequence: it changes a concrete implementation choice in DESIGN.md.

If any proof is missing, omit the claim. Do not turn a visual impression into a token, a single occurrence into a site-wide rule, or a guessed value into YAML. Exact values require computed styles or loaded CSS; otherwise describe the role without a value or omit it.

## 3. Decide what belongs

In repository mode, find explicit product intent or a design reference before describing product character. In URL mode, do not invent product character; the Overview may state only the site's observable purpose and presentation, and must identify the document as reconstructed.

Write YAML only from named shared tokens and roles in governing sources. Do not turn utility classes, repeated literals, or component values into token scales.

Treat frontmatter shape as a hard gate, not a stylistic choice: a value that is a token group must be a mapping whose children are the schema's fields. Never emit scalar typography entries (`sans: Geist`), arbitrary nested source objects (`font-family: { mono: ... }`), or rounded keys copied from CSS variable names (`radius-sm`, `radius-md`, etc.).

Use mappings, never sequences, for token groups. When a governing source defines one group-level token such as `--radius`, normalize it to `base`; otherwise preserve the source token names.

Map source values into DESIGN.md schema fields. Preserve semantic token names, not source object nesting. For example, write `typography.mono.fontFamily: Geist Mono`, never `typography.mono: Geist Mono`; write `rounded.base: 0.625rem` when the source has only `--radius`, never `rounded.radius` or derived radius steps.

Resolve framework utilities through the active theme or configuration before writing exact values.

Identify the repository's export target before writing frontmatter: `css-tailwind` for Tailwind v4, `json-tailwind` for Tailwind v3, and `dtcg` otherwise. Token names must be valid for that target.

Check the installed DESIGN.md specification before encoding theme modes:

```bash
npx @google/design.md spec
```

If the specification supports `themes` and `default-theme`, use its theme-aware token syntax. Otherwise, put the default-theme value under each canonical semantic token and preserve exact alternate-theme values in a `## Themes` table. Do not create parallel `-light` and `-dark` token names, discard alternate-theme values, or use unreleased syntax. A fallback Themes table is documentation only; do not pretend it makes the frontmatter theme-aware.

In repository mode, every prose rule must be supported by explicit guidance, a named shared token or variant, or a shared owner used by at least two audited surfaces. Otherwise omit it.

In URL mode, every prose rule must be directly observable. A site-wide rule must recur across at least two sampled templates; otherwise scope it to the inspected page. Use reconstructed role-based names and label the document as a draft.

URL-mode YAML is intentionally sparse, but not empty when measured evidence exists. Add a category when at least one supported value or role survives the three-proof gate. Colors may use computed values or verified public custom properties, but must remain flat and export-safe; typography must use canonical fields such as `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, and `fontWeight`; rounded and spacing values must come from computed styles or loaded declarations. Do not create aliases such as `primary`, `elevated`, or `display` merely to organize observations. A component section requires the same interaction or surface treatment to recur across at least two sampled pages and to change a concrete implementation choice.

URL reconstruction does not change the frontmatter schema. Use only these typography property names: `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `fontWeight`, and `letterSpacing`. For example:

```yaml
typography:
  sans:
    fontFamily: Inter Variable
  display:
    fontFamily: Inter Variable
    fontSize: 64px
    lineHeight: 64px
    fontWeight: 510
```

Never emit URL-specific aliases such as `family`, `size`, `weight`, `mobile-display`, or nested `sans`/`mono` values inside a typography scale. Reconstructed role names may vary; schema field names may not.

For URL output, use `css-tailwind` as the compatibility export target unless the user specifies another target. Flatten reconstructed color roles into valid token names. Use `background-primary`, `foreground-secondary`, or `border-muted`, not nested keys such as `background.primary` or `foreground.secondary`. Every emitted token name must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$`; reject and rewrite any key that would fail this test.

Normalize URL frontmatter before writing any Markdown. The order is: collect evidence, choose the export target, map evidence into the canonical schema, reject invalid shapes, then write the document. Never draft prose first and retrofit the YAML afterward.

URL frontmatter must satisfy these shape rules:

- `colors` is a flat mapping of valid token names to values.
- `typography` is a mapping of named scales; each scale is a mapping using only canonical fields.
- `rounded` and `spacing` are flat mappings of valid token names to values.
- `components` may reference canonical token paths but may not introduce a second token schema.

If normalization would require inventing a token name, field, scale, or semantic relationship, omit the candidate.

Outside the Overview, every Markdown sentence must change an implementation choice. Delete component inventories, generic design advice, and prose that only restates YAML.

Preserve the scope and direction of every rule. When implementation conflicts with explicit guidance, document the guidance and report the conflict outside `DESIGN.md`.

## 4. Write the document

Start with the smallest valid frontmatter:

```yaml
---
version: alpha
name: <string>
description: <string>
---
```

Only `name` is required. Add `colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, or `components` only when a governing source already defines that named system or contract. Do not create token names to organize implementation values. Token references use `{path.to.token}`.

Use schema-shaped mappings, not copied source nesting. A typography scale is always named and maps its properties beneath it:

```yaml
typography:
  sans:
    fontFamily: Geist
  mono:
    fontFamily: Geist Mono
```

If the source defines only `--radius`, write `rounded.base`, not `rounded.radius`; do not derive `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or `xl` from utility classes or repeated values. Before saving, inspect the parsed frontmatter and reject it yourself if any `typography` child is scalar or if `rounded` contains keys not present in the governing source.

Start with `## Overview`. State only the product's purpose and evidenced design direction. Do not summarize pages, components, tokens, or implementation. Add only supported sections from this order:

1. Colors
2. Themes
3. Typography
4. Layout
5. Elevation & Depth
6. Shapes
7. Components
8. Do's and Don'ts

Do not create a section merely because it exists in the format. Do not reorder or duplicate included sections. Add an unknown section only when supported guidance cannot fit a standard section.

Markdown records design intent and application guidance. Except for the fallback `## Themes` table, do not put token inventories, component configuration, source syntax, or documentation methodology in Markdown.

Include a Don't only when a governing source states an explicit prohibition.

- Put exact normative values in YAML frontmatter, except alternate-theme values when the installed specification cannot represent modes.
- Put supported rationale and application guidance in Markdown.
- Preserve accepted decisions from an existing `DESIGN.md` unless the user or current governing evidence replaces them.
- Do not invent brand personality, audience, or emotional rationale.
- Do not include citations, audit notes, rejected candidates, conflicts, or unresolved questions inside `DESIGN.md`.

Before saving, delete:

- any YAML token not already named by a governing source
- any page-local behavior presented as a product-wide rule
- any implementation pattern that conflicts with explicit guidance
- any prohibition not explicitly stated
- any exact implementation value outside YAML frontmatter or the fallback `## Themes` table
- any component configuration or documentation methodology in Markdown
- any sentence that does not change the resulting DESIGN.md

Run one final no-op pass: remove vague advice such as “be thorough,” “keep it polished,” or “use good judgment.” Keep only evidence gates, schema constraints, or application rules that change the document.

## 5. Validate

Run structural linting:

```bash
npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md
```

Then run one compatibility export using the target selected above:

```bash
npx @google/design.md export --format <format> DESIGN.md
```

Inspect the output. Every populated frontmatter category supported by the target must emit its corresponding token category; an empty or missing category is a schema failure even when the command exits successfully. Rewrite the frontmatter and rerun validation until the category is emitted, unless the target genuinely cannot represent it. Do not report success while any populated category is missing from the export. Do not return the document while lint or export fails. Do not remove supported design information solely to satisfy an exporter limitation; report that limitation instead. Do not create or retain exported files.

For `css-tailwind`, verify these output families: `colors` → `--color-*`, `typography.<name>.fontFamily` → `--font-*`, `typography.<name>.fontSize` → `--text-*`, `rounded` → `--radius-*`, and `spacing` → `--spacing-*`. Typography entries are named scales; put `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, and `lineHeight` inside each scale, never under arbitrary source nesting such as `font-family`. If `typography` is populated but the export contains neither `--font-*` nor `--text-*`, the document is invalid and must be rewritten before reporting.

When updating an existing document, preserve its original contents temporarily and run:

```bash
npx @google/design.md diff <previous-file> DESIGN.md
```

Restore any removed accepted decision unless current governing evidence or the user explicitly replaces it.

## 6. Report

Return:

- mode and audited product or URL
- created or updated `DESIGN.md`
- governing sources used
- conflicts or unsupported areas omitted from the document
- final lint and export results

In URL mode, label the output as a reconstructed draft.

If validation reports an invalid shape or missing export category, rewrite the frontmatter and rerun; if the category cannot be repaired, remove it and report it as omitted.

## 2. Trace the evidence

In repository mode, inspect in this order:

1. Existing `DESIGN.md` and explicit repository guidance
2. Tokens, themes, variables, and global styles
3. Shared primitives and their variants
4. Representative routes and rendered consumers
5. Surface-local implementations

A source participates only when the selected product imports, references, inherits, or renders it. Exclude proposals, migrations, examples, generated outputs, legacy implementations, and similarly named packages unless the selected product uses them.

In URL mode, sample representative elements for:

- colors and surface roles
- typography roles
- spacing and layout
- borders, radii, and elevation
- navigation, buttons, inputs, cards, and repeated content structures
- desktop and mobile presentation

Prefer computed values and loaded CSS declarations over visual estimation.

Before drafting URL-mode prose or YAML, build a private evidence ledger for each sampled page and viewport. For each candidate, record: page, viewport, element role, computed property/value, and the matching loaded-CSS declaration or custom property when available. Inspect the public stylesheets loaded by the page, including custom properties and media-query rules; a stylesheet value is usable only when it is connected to a rendered element or recurs across the sampled pages.

Promote a URL value into DESIGN.md when either (a) the rendered computed value and a loaded declaration/custom property agree, or (b) the same computed value recurs for the same role across the required samples. If neither condition holds, omit the value. You may preserve an exposed custom-property name only when its declaration and rendered use are directly observable; do not invent semantic aliases from a raw value.

For every URL-mode claim, require all three proofs before writing it:

1. Observation: the pattern or value is visible or computed on the rendered page.
2. Basis: it is measured, or recurs across the required sampled pages/viewports.
3. Consequence: it changes a concrete implementation choice in DESIGN.md.

If any proof is missing, omit the claim. Do not turn a visual impression into a token, a single occurrence into a site-wide rule, or a guessed value into YAML. Exact values require computed styles or loaded CSS; otherwise describe the role without a value or omit it.

## 3. Decide what belongs

In repository mode, find explicit product intent or a design reference before describing product character. In URL mode, do not invent product character; the Overview may state only the site's observable purpose and presentation, and must identify the document as reconstructed.

Write YAML only from named shared tokens and roles in governing sources. Do not turn utility classes, repeated literals, or component values into token scales.

Treat frontmatter shape as a hard gate, not a stylistic choice: a value that is a token group must be a mapping whose children are the schema's fields. Never emit scalar typography entries (`sans: Geist`), arbitrary nested source objects (`font-family: { mono: ... }`), or rounded keys copied from CSS variable names (`radius-sm`, `radius-md`, etc.).

Use mappings, never sequences, for token groups. When a governing source defines one group-level token such as `--radius`, normalize it to `base`; otherwise preserve the source token names.

Map source values into DESIGN.md schema fields. Preserve semantic token names, not source object nesting. For example, write `typography.mono.fontFamily: Geist Mono`, never `typography.mono: Geist Mono`; write `rounded.base: 0.625rem` when the source has only `--radius`, never `rounded.radius` or derived radius steps.

Resolve framework utilities through the active theme or configuration before writing exact values.

Identify the repository's export target before writing frontmatter: `css-tailwind` for Tailwind v4, `json-tailwind` for Tailwind v3, and `dtcg` otherwise. Token names must be valid for that target.

Check the installed DESIGN.md specification before encoding theme modes:

```bash
npx @google/design.md spec
```

If the specification supports `themes` and `default-theme`, use its theme-aware token syntax. Otherwise, put the default-theme value under each canonical semantic token and preserve exact alternate-theme values in a `## Themes` table. Do not create parallel `-light` and `-dark` token names, discard alternate-theme values, or use unreleased syntax. A fallback Themes table is documentation only; do not pretend it makes the frontmatter theme-aware.

In repository mode, every prose rule must be supported by explicit guidance, a named shared token or variant, or a shared owner used by at least two audited surfaces. Otherwise omit it.

In URL mode, every prose rule must be directly observable. A site-wide rule must recur across at least two sampled templates; otherwise scope it to the inspected page. Use reconstructed role-based names and label the document as a draft.

URL-mode YAML is intentionally sparse, but not empty when measured evidence exists. Add a category when at least one supported value or role survives the three-proof gate. Colors may use computed values or verified public custom properties, but must remain flat and export-safe; typography must use canonical fields such as `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, and `fontWeight`; rounded and spacing values must come from computed styles or loaded declarations. Do not create aliases such as `primary`, `elevated`, or `display` merely to organize observations. A component section requires the same interaction or surface treatment to recur across at least two sampled pages and to change a concrete implementation choice.

URL reconstruction does not change the frontmatter schema. Use only these typography property names: `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `fontWeight`, and `letterSpacing`. For example:

```yaml
typography:
  sans:
    fontFamily: Inter Variable
  display:
    fontFamily: Inter Variable
    fontSize: 64px
    lineHeight: 64px
    fontWeight: 510
```

Never emit URL-specific aliases such as `family`, `size`, `weight`, `mobile-display`, or nested `sans`/`mono` values inside a typography scale. Reconstructed role names may vary; schema field names may not.

For URL output, use `css-tailwind` as the compatibility export target unless the user specifies another target. Flatten reconstructed color roles into valid token names. Use `background-primary`, `foreground-secondary`, or `border-muted`, not nested keys such as `background.primary` or `foreground.secondary`. Every emitted token name must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$`; reject and rewrite any key that would fail this test.

Normalize URL frontmatter before writing any Markdown. The order is: collect evidence, choose the export target, map evidence into the canonical schema, reject invalid shapes, then write the document. Never draft prose first and retrofit the YAML afterward.

URL frontmatter must satisfy these shape rules:

- `colors` is a flat mapping of valid token names to values.
- `typography` is a mapping of named scales; each scale is a mapping using only canonical fields.
- `rounded` and `spacing` are flat mappings of valid token names to values.
- `components` may reference canonical token paths but may not introduce a second token schema.

If normalization would require inventing a token name, field, scale, or semantic relationship, omit the candidate.

Outside the Overview, every Markdown sentence must change an implementation choice. Delete component inventories, generic design advice, and prose that only restates YAML.

Preserve the scope and direction of every rule. When implementation conflicts with explicit guidance, document the guidance and report the conflict outside `DESIGN.md`.

## 4. Write the document

Start with the smallest valid frontmatter:

```yaml
---
version: alpha
name: <string>
description: <string>
---
```

Only `name` is required. Add `colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, or `components` only when a governing source already defines that named system or contract. Do not create token names to organize implementation values. Token references use `{path.to.token}`.

Use schema-shaped mappings, not copied source nesting. A typography scale is always named and maps its properties beneath it:

```yaml
typography:
  sans:
    fontFamily: Geist
  mono:
    fontFamily: Geist Mono
```

If the source defines only `--radius`, write `rounded.base`, not `rounded.radius`; do not derive `sm`, `md`, `lg`, or `xl` from utility classes or repeated values. Before saving, inspect the parsed frontmatter and reject it yourself if any `typography` child is scalar or if `rounded` contains keys not present in the governing source.

Start with `## Overview`. State only the product's purpose and evidenced design direction. Do not summarize pages, components, tokens, or implementation. Add only supported sections from this order:

1. Colors
2. Themes
3. Typography
4. Layout
5. Elevation & Depth
6. Shapes
7. Components
8. Do's and Don'ts

Do not create a section merely because it exists in the format. Do not reorder or duplicate included sections. Add an unknown section only when supported guidance cannot fit a standard section.

Markdown records design intent and application guidance. Except for the fallback `## Themes` table, do not put token inventories, component configuration, source syntax, or documentation methodology in Markdown.

Include a Don't only when a governing source states an explicit prohibition.

- Put exact normative values in YAML frontmatter, except alternate-theme values when the installed specification cannot represent modes.
- Put supported rationale and application guidance in Markdown.
- Preserve accepted decisions from an existing `DESIGN.md` unless the user or current governing evidence replaces them.
- Do not invent brand personality, audience, or emotional rationale.
- Do not include citations, audit notes, rejected candidates, conflicts, or unresolved questions inside `DESIGN.md`.

Before saving, delete:

- any YAML token not already named by a governing source
- any page-local behavior presented as a product-wide rule
- any implementation pattern that conflicts with explicit guidance
- any prohibition not explicitly stated
- any exact implementation value outside YAML frontmatter or the fallback `## Themes` table
- any component configuration or documentation methodology in Markdown
- any sentence that does not change the resulting DESIGN.md

Run one final no-op pass: remove vague advice such as “be thorough,” “keep it polished,” or “use good judgment.” Keep only evidence gates, schema constraints, or application rules that change the document.

## 5. Validate

Run structural linting:

```bash
npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md
```

Then run one compatibility export using the target selected above:

```bash
npx @google/design.md export --format <format> DESIGN.md
```

Inspect the output. Every populated frontmatter category supported by the target must emit its corresponding token category; an empty or missing category is a schema failure even when the command exits successfully. Rewrite the frontmatter and rerun validation until the category is emitted, unless the target genuinely cannot represent it. Do not report success while any populated category is missing from the export. Do not return the document while lint or export fails. Do not remove supported design information solely to satisfy an exporter limitation; report that limitation instead. Do not create or retain exported files.

For `css-tailwind`, verify these output families: `colors` → `--color-*`, `typography.<name>.fontFamily` → `--font-*`, `typography.<name>.fontSize` → `--text-*`, `rounded` → `--radius-*`, and `spacing` → `--spacing-*`. Typography entries are named scales; put `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, and `lineHeight` inside each scale, never under arbitrary source nesting such as `font-family`. If `typography` is populated but the export contains neither `--font-*` nor `--text-*`, the document is invalid and must be rewritten before reporting.

When updating an existing document, preserve its original contents temporarily and run:

```bash
npx @google/design.md diff <previous-file> DESIGN.md
```

Restore any removed accepted decision unless current governing evidence or the user explicitly replaces it.

## 6. Report

Return:

- mode and audited product or URL
- created or updated `DESIGN.md`
- governing sources used
- conflicts or unsupported areas omitted from the document
- final lint and export results

In URL mode, label the output as a reconstructed draft.

skills.body:
---
name: device-frames
description: Create device-framed screenshots, product images, videos, or live UI mockups. Use when placing an image, recording, webpage, or component inside a phone, foldable, tablet, watch, laptop, monitor, or browser frame, including App Store-style visuals and launch videos.
---

# Device frames

Create the requested image, video, or live component using the project's tools and conventions.
Do not assume a frame library, scripts, server, or browser is available.

## Start with the deliverable

- Determine the device, orientation, content, output format, background, and dimensions. Use
  sensible defaults; ask only when a missing choice materially changes the result.
- Use the supplied screenshot, recording, page, or component. If none is provided, use a blank
  screen or simple original placeholder.
- Build a live component, render an image, or composite a video as requested. Keep the device
  static unless animation is requested.
- Check available tools first. Ask before adding dependencies or changing unrelated project code.

## Construct the frame

Draw the screen and hardware as separate layers with CSS and SVG or equivalent vector tools.

1. Lay out content at the screen's native aspect ratio, then scale the entire device uniformly.
   Never stretch media: use `cover` to crop or `contain` to preserve it. Report cropping.
2. Draw the outer case, bezel, glass, controls, stand, and camera separately from the screen.
   Clip the screen to its display outline. Keep cutouts above screen content and keep the screen
   rectangle distinct from the device's full bounding box.
3. Use continuous rounded corners for modern handhelds. Position buttons, camera, and hinge
   for the selected device and orientation. An open foldable has one continuous inner screen;
   do not insert a gap at the hinge.
4. Give metal, glass, and shadows restrained tonal variation. Keep backgrounds clean and support
   transparency when requested. Do not add manufacturer logos or imply endorsement.
5. Add status bars, home indicators, or other system UI only when requested and not already in
   the source. Synthetic furniture is an approximation, not native system UI.

For landscape, rotate the hardware and screen geometry together while keeping content upright.
Account for iframe restrictions and loading failures when embedding pages.

## Device geometry

Use logical points for layout. Output pixels depend on scale and pixel density, not necessarily
the physical panel resolution.

Use these sizes for the corresponding device; check current official specifications when needed.

| Device                              | Screen in points, width × height | Distinctive details                                                             |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| iPhone 17 or 18 Pro                 | 402 × 874                        | Rounded screen, Dynamic Island                                                  |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max                   | 440 × 956                        | Rounded screen, Dynamic Island                                                  |
| iPhone Air                          | 420 × 912                        | Rounded screen, Dynamic Island                                                  |
| iPhone Duo, closed                  | 466 × 678                        | Short, wide outer screen; camera near the upper-right corner; hinge on the left |
| iPhone Duo, fully open              | 951 × 669, inferred              | Wide inner screen; central hinge; under-display camera hidden while inactive    |
| iPad Pro 11-inch                    | 834 × 1210                       | Even bezel; camera in the long bezel                                            |
| iPad Pro 13-inch                    | 1032 × 1376                      | Even bezel; camera in the long bezel                                            |
| Apple Watch Series 12, 46 mm        | 208 × 248                        | Rounded case, side crown, optional strap                                        |
| Apple Watch Series 12, 42 mm        | 187 × 223                        | Rounded case, side crown, optional strap                                        |
| MacBook Pro 14-inch, M6             | 1512 × 982                       | Thin bezel, centred top notch, metal base                                       |
| MacBook Pro 16-inch, PROLED XDR     | 1736 × 1133                      | Thin bezel, rounded display, small camera cutout within the screen              |
| MacBook Neo 13-inch                 | 1204 × 753                       | Rounded top display corners, camera in bezel, no notch                          |
| Studio Display / Studio Display XDR | 2560 × 1440                      | 27-inch 5K panel at 2×; black bezel and aluminium stand                         |

The Duo open-screen value is derived from Apple's 2853 × 2007 App Store screenshot size at 3×.
Apple lists the physical inner panel as 2670 × 1878 pixels; screenshot dimensions do not by
themselves establish its logical viewport. Treat 951 × 669 as an approximation, not a verified
native point size. Closed and fully open frames do not simulate folding, split-screen, reserved
regions, or changes in iOS layout.

For Duo app visuals, consult Apple's
[design guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-iphone-duo).
The outer camera remains visible; the inner camera is hidden until active. System controls are
typically arranged along the side on the outer display and the open display in landscape. Avoid
placing key content beneath them; real screenshots should keep their own system UI.

### Fully open Duo: one screen, not two phones

- Draw **one wide case, one bezel, and one uninterrupted inner display**. The display is a
  single rounded rectangle: only its four outer corners are rounded. It spans the centre at
  the same full height as the rest of the screen.
- Use a **951 × 669 screen rectangle** before scaling: width ÷ height is approximately **1.422**.
  The whole case is approximately **992.6 × 710.4**, or **1.397:1**. Do not make either shape
  square or fit it to the output canvas; add transparent padding around the uniformly scaled frame
  instead. These are the default fully open, unrotated dimensions, not two portrait screens.
- Do not draw a central black bar, a visible cylindrical hinge, a gap, two screen panels, or
  rounded corners at the centre. If the case needs a hinge detail, restrict it to the thin
  enclosure outside the display at the top and bottom; do not cover the active display.
- The inner camera is behind the display and invisible by default. The outer-display camera,
  Dynamic Island, and conventional phone side-button arrangement do not appear on the open
  inner screen.
- Build the frame with deterministic vector geometry, not generative image synthesis. Image
  generators can invent hinges and proportions even when prompted not to. Composite supplied
  content separately. If no vector or programmatic rendering tool is available, report the
  limitation rather than substituting an AI-generated device.
- For a plain grey screen, use one opaque, solid grey fill such as `#d8d8dc`. Do not add screen
  gradients, noise, reflections, folds, or texture unless requested. Keep hinge marks tiny and
  outside the active screen.
- Before delivery, measure the rendered **screen bounds**, not the whole PNG: width ÷ height
  should be within 1% of `951 / 669`. Check that the centre and both halves are one continuous
  display, with no camera by default. If the ratio or shape is wrong, fix and rerender it.

For other devices, consult official specifications and hardware references, or label the result
as an approximation. Screen dimensions alone do not establish hardware accuracy.

## Measured hardware

For physical fidelity, consult the manufacturer's dimensional drawing or a front-view reference.
Keep display size, case size, camera and button positions in one coordinate system. Scale
millimetres by
`screen width in points / active display width in mm`; position the screen using the active-area
inset. Preserve non-symmetric corners and hardware offsets. Never ship the manufacturer's drawing
or marketing imagery as part of the frame.

Starting measurements in millimetres; camera centres are measured from the case's top-left.
Verify them against the current drawing.

| Device             | Case W × H      | Active display W × H | Camera                                                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| iPhone 17          | 71.45 × 149.61  | 66.57 × 144.79       | Island centre (35.725, 7.79), 20.74 × 6.07                                   |
| iPhone Air         | 74.70 × 156.18  | 69.55 × 151.03       | Island centre (37.35, 8.0), 20.76 × 6.07                                     |
| iPhone 18 Pro      | 71.85 × 150.01  | 66.57 × 144.73       | Island centre (35.925, 7.99), 15.66 × 6.07                                   |
| iPhone 18 Pro Max  | 77.98 × 163.43  | 72.86 × 158.31       | Island centre (38.99, 7.91), 15.68 × 6.07                                    |
| iPhone Duo, closed | 84.10 × 117.80  | 77.17 × 112.28       | Hole centre (73.39, 10.62), diameter 6.07                                    |
| iPhone Duo, open   | 164.60 × 117.80 | 157.70 × 110.90      | Under-display camera centre (115.8, 10.55), diameter 4.32; hidden by default |
| iPad Pro 11-inch   | 177.51 × 249.70 | 160.13 × 232.32      | In the long bezel                                                            |
| iPad Pro 13-inch   | 215.53 × 281.58 | 199.14 × 265.19      | In the long bezel                                                            |
| Watch 46 mm        | 40.28 × 46.38   | 32.45 × 38.69        | No front camera                                                              |
| Watch 42 mm        | 36.95 × 42.57   | 29.17 × 34.79        | No front camera                                                              |

### Insets, corners, and controls

For the table above, centre the active rectangle in the case unless otherwise stated. The closed
Duo is asymmetric: place its active rectangle 4.17 mm from the left and 2.76 mm from the top;
place its 79.93 × 115.04 mm glass 2.79 mm from the left and 1.38 mm from the top. For the open
Duo, centre the active rectangle; its hinge is at x = 82.3 mm. Its inner glass inset is assumed
to be approximately 1.33 mm horizontally and 1.38 mm vertically.

These outer-corner profiles are `[x, y]` offsets in millimetres from the corner's top-left
extreme, ordered from the top edge to the side. Mirror them into the other corners. Interpolate
smoothly through the points; inset the outline for the glass and screen. Inset curves and
unpublished display corners are approximations.

- iPhone 17: `[19.23,0] [14.53,0.02] [9.87,0.48] [5.56,2.26] [2.26,5.56] [0.48,9.87] [0.02,14.53] [0,19.23]`.
- iPhone Air: `[19.36,0] [13.85,0.04] [8.43,0.91] [3.78,3.78]`, then mirror across x=y.
- iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: `[19.43,0] [13.9,0.04] [8.46,0.92] [3.8,3.8]`, then mirror across x=y.
- Duo outer corners: `[17.3,0] [12.44,0.06] [7.68,1] [3.62,3.63] [1,7.68] [0.02,12.44] [0,17.31]`.
  Closed hinge-side corners instead use `[3.03,0] [2.52,0.02] [2.06,0.23] [1.82,0.67] [1.8,1.19] [0.92,1.36] [0.26,1.96] [0.01,2.82] [0,3.72]`.
- iPad Pro case corners: `[15.9,0] [14.28,0.02] [13.27,0.1] [11.77,0.3] [10.48,0.6] [9.16,1] [7.68,1.6] [6.38,2.4] [5.01,3.4] [4.85,4.85]`, then mirror across x=y. Display corners start at `[5.6,0] [5.04,0.02] [4.5,0.1] [3.64,0.3] [2.87,0.6] [2.11,1] [1.49,1.49]`, then mirror.
- Watch case corners: approximate with a continuous curve; use an outer tangent distance of
  about 20.14 mm for 46 mm and 18.48 mm for 42 mm. The display is inset and has tighter corners.

Button centres below are measured from the top for side buttons and from the left for top buttons;
length and protrusion are in millimetres. A flush button can be omitted in a straight-on view.

- iPhone 17 and Air: left centres 34.08, 48.23, 62.43; lengths 6.9, 11.2, 11.2. Right centre
  55.32 (Air 55.33), length 17.7 (Air 17.8). Protrusion 0.45.
- iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: left centres 34.28, 48.43, 62.63; lengths 6.9, 11.2, 11.2. Right
  centre 55.53, length 17.7. Protrusion 0.45.
- Duo closed: top centres 44.35 and 57.73, length 10.88; right centre 42.87, length 18.68.
  Protrusion 0.45. For the open view, approximate the top centres by adding 82.3; retain the
  right-side position.
- iPad Pro: right centres 19.33 and 31.39, length 10.06; top centre approximately case width minus
  20.01, length 12.06. Protrusion approximately 0.4.
- Watch: right crown length 7, protrusion 2.27; centre at half case height minus 8.26 (46 mm) or
  8.23 (42 mm). Strap colour and dimensions may be adapted to the requested band.

### Laptop and display proportions

These front-view values are **visual approximations in screen points**, not measured hardware.
For laptops, `side / top / bottom` are black bezel widths; `edge` is the metal rim; base
overhang is per side. The screen is inside the bezel, not the entire lid.

| Frame | Bezel side / top / bottom | Edge | Lid corner | Screen corner | Camera or notch | Base overhang / height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MacBook Pro 14-inch | 16 / 16 / 22 | 4 | 24 | 12, top only | centred top notch 196 × 32 | 50 / 38 |
| MacBook Pro 16-inch PROLED | 14 / 14 / 18 | 4 | 30 | 24, all four | centred 56 × 27 capsule, 14 below screen top | 55 / 38 |
| MacBook Neo 13-inch | 30 / 30 / 60 | 5 | 42 | 20, top only | small camera in top bezel; no notch | 105 / 42 |

The lid's two hinge-side corners are tighter than the top ones: 6 points. The black glass is
the lid inset by `edge`, with corners `lid corner − edge` on top and 3 points at the hinge.
A notch hangs from the screen's top edge with 10-point bottom corners and a 3.5-point camera
dot; a bezel camera is a 3-point dot centred in the top bezel.

For Studio Display and Studio Display XDR, start with a 2560 × 1440 screen, a 57-point black
bezel and 3-point metal edge on each side, 18-point outer corner radius, and a centred stand
about 655 points wide and 498 points tall. Apple publishes a 62.3 × 36.2 cm enclosure for both;
stand shape, bezel width, and details above are approximations.

### Coordinate example

For the closed Duo, `k = 466 / 77.17 ≈ 6.0386` points/mm. With the case at `(0, 0)`, the
approximate screen rectangle starts at `(4.17k, 2.76k)` and is `466 × 678` points. Draw the
case at `84.1k × 117.8k`, then draw the camera centred at `(73.39k, 10.62k)` with diameter
`6.07k`. Apply the asymmetric hinge-side corner profile on the left. Keep the camera in case
coordinates, not screen coordinates; subtract the screen origin if positioning it inside the
screen. Include any button protrusion when computing the exported bounding box.

For the **open Duo**, use `k = 951 / 157.7 ≈ 6.0304` points/mm. Draw one case of approximately
`992.6 × 710.4` points. Centre one `951 × 669` screen at approximately `(20.8, 20.7)` inside
the case. The centre of the screen is approximately `x = 496.3` in case coordinates: it is
screen content, not a seam or an extra bezel. The actual active-area height and inferred logical
screen height differ slightly after scaling; centre the logical rectangle within the measured
active area. Any hinge details belong outside the active screen.

Use [Apple's dimensional drawings](https://developer.apple.com/accessories/dimensional-drawings/)
for specific corner profiles, insets and button details, and the relevant manufacturer's product
specification for physical screen pixels. Screen resolution alone does not verify the shape of a
frame. If no suitable front reference is available, approximate the shape and say so; never call
it pixel-perfect without a comparison.

## Output and verification

- **Image:** render at the requested pixel dimensions, including transparent alpha if requested.
  Wait for images, fonts, and page content to load; surface failures instead of delivering an
  empty screen. Keep the original content's aspect ratio. For transparent output, check that
  pixels outside the hardware have alpha 0; the presence of an alpha channel alone is not enough.
- **Video:** fit the recording to the screen, apply the exact same screen clip or mask as the
  frame, and layer hardware above it. Preserve timing and audio when possible. For transparency,
  choose a codec and container that actually support alpha; do not assume MP4 does. Check the
  resulting file rather than inferring its codec from the extension.
- **Live UI:** keep the screen interactive where requested. Do not intercept its input with
  decorative hardware layers; scale the frame and its hit areas together. Respect the existing
  project's accessibility and layout conventions.
- Inspect the actual image or representative video frames before delivery. Check clipping, camera
  placement, frame edges, source content, scale, colour, transparency, and any requested
  orientation. If visual inspection or playback is unavailable, say so.
- Report the output path or component, dimensions, cropping or approximations, and checks actually
  performed. Do not claim pixel-perfect accuracy based only on screen dimensions.

## Device geometry

  Dynamic Island, and conventional phone side-button arrangement do not appear on the open

  generators can invent hinges and proportions even when prompted not to. Composite supplied
  content separately. If no vector or programmatic rendering tool is available, report the
  limitation rather than substituting an AI-generated device.

  gradients, noise, reflections, folds, or texture unless requested. Keep hinge marks tiny and
  outside the active screen.

  should be within 1% of `951 / 669`. Check that the centre and both halves are one continuous

For physical fidelity, consult the manufacturer's dimensional drawing or a front-view reference.

millimetres by
`screen width in points / active display width in mm`; position the screen using the active-area
inset. Preserve non-symmetric corners and hardware offsets. Never ship the manufacturer's drawing
or marketing imagery as part of the frame.

| iPhone Air         | 74.70 × 156.18  | 69.55 × 151.03       | Island centre (37.35, 8.0), 20.76 × 6.07                                     |
| iPhone 18 Pro      | 71.85 × 150.01  | 66.57 × 144.73       | Island centre (35.925, 7.99), 15.66 × 6.07                                   |

active area. Any hinge details belong outside the active screen.

  pixels outside the hardware have alpha 0; the presence of an alpha channel alone is not enough.
- **Video:** fit the recording to the screen, apply the exact same screen clip or mask as the
  frame, and layer hardware above it. Preserve timing and audio when possible. For transparency,
  choose a codec and container that actually support alpha; do not assume MP4 does. Check the
  resulting file rather than inferring its codec from the extension.
- **Live UI:** keep the screen interactive where requested. Do not intercept its input with
  decorative hardware layers; scale the frame and its hit areas together. Respect the existing
  project's accessibility and layout conventions.
- Inspect the actual image or representative video frames before delivery. Check clipping, camera
  placement, frame edges, source content, scale, colour, transparency, and any requested
  orientation. If visual inspection or playback is unavailable, say so.
- Report the output path or component, dimensions, cropping or approximations, and checks actually
  performed. Do not claim pixel-perfect accuracy based only on screen dimensions.

skills.desc: Audit and fix HTML metadata including page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph tags, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD structured data, and robots directives. skills.body:
---
name: fixing-metadata
description: >
  Audit and fix HTML metadata including page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph
  tags, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD structured data, and robots directives. Use when adding
  SEO metadata, fixing social share previews, reviewing Open Graph tags, setting up canonical URLs,
  or shipping new pages that need correct meta tags.
version: 1.0.1
license: MIT
---

## Workflow

1. Identify pages with missing or incorrect metadata (titles, descriptions, canonical, OG tags)
2. Audit against the priority rules below — fix critical issues (duplicates, indexing) first
3. Ensure title, description, canonical, and og:url all agree with each other
4. Verify social cards render correctly on a real URL, not localhost
5. Keep diffs minimal and scoped to metadata only — do not refactor unrelated code
## when to apply

Reference these guidelines when:
- adding or changing page titles, descriptions, canonical, robots
- implementing Open Graph or Twitter card metadata
- setting favicons, app icons, manifest, theme-color
- building shared SEO components or layout metadata defaults
- adding structured data (JSON-LD)
- changing locale, alternate languages, or canonical routing
- shipping new pages, marketing pages, or shareable links

## rule categories by priority

| priority | category | impact |
|----------|----------|--------|
| 1 | correctness and duplication | critical |
| 2 | title and description | high |
| 3 | canonical and indexing | high |
| 4 | social cards | high |
| 5 | icons and manifest | medium |
| 6 | structured data | medium |
| 7 | locale and alternates | low-medium |
| 8 | tool boundaries | critical |

## quick reference

### 1. correctness and duplication (critical)

- define metadata in one place per page, avoid competing systems
- do not emit duplicate title, description, canonical, or robots tags
- metadata must be deterministic, no random or unstable values
- escape and sanitize any user-generated or dynamic strings
- every page must have safe defaults for title and description

### 2. title and description (high)

- every page must have a title
- use a consistent title format across the site
- keep titles short and readable, avoid stuffing
- shareable or searchable pages should have a meta description
- descriptions must be plain text, no markdown or quote spam

### 3. canonical and indexing (high)

- canonical must point to the preferred URL for the page
- use noindex only for private, duplicate, or non-public pages
- robots meta must match actual access intent
- previews or staging pages should be noindex by default when possible
- paginated pages must have correct canonical behavior

### 4. social cards (high)

- shareable pages must set Open Graph title, description, and image
- Open Graph and Twitter images must use absolute URLs
- prefer correct image dimensions and stable aspect ratios
- og:url must match the canonical URL
- use a sensible og:type, usually website or article
- set twitter:card appropriately, summary_large_image by default

### 5. icons and manifest (medium)

- include at least one favicon that works across browsers
- include apple-touch-icon when relevant
- manifest must be valid and referenced when used
- set theme-color intentionally to avoid mismatched UI chrome
- icon paths should be stable and cacheable

### 6. structured data (medium)

- do not add JSON-LD unless it clearly maps to real page content
- JSON-LD must be valid and reflect what is actually rendered
- do not invent ratings, reviews, prices, or organization details
- prefer one structured data block per page unless required

### 7. locale and alternates (low-medium)

- set the html lang attribute correctly
- set og:locale when localization exists
- add hreflang alternates only when pages truly exist
- localized pages must canonicalize correctly per locale

### 8. tool boundaries (critical)

- prefer minimal changes, do not refactor unrelated code
- do not migrate frameworks or SEO libraries unless requested
- follow the project's existing metadata pattern (Next.js metadata API, react-helmet, manual head, etc.)

## review guidance

- fix critical issues first (duplicates, canonical, indexing)
- ensure title, description, canonical, and og:url agree
- verify social cards on a real URL, not localhost
- prefer stable, boring metadata over clever or dynamic
- keep diffs minimal and scoped to metadata only
